page: Amazon Web Services g6.16xlarge is a graphics-intensive virtual machine powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features an AMD EPYC 7R13 processor with 64 vCPUs and 32 physical cores running at 3.4 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The system is equipped with 256.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, a single NVIDIA Ada Lovelace L4 GPU with 22 GB of VRAM, and 1880 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. Network connectivity is rated at a baseline of 25 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate strong performance across multiple domains. The server ranks in the top 25% for stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU tests, as well as Geekbench multi-core, ray tracing, and image processing workloads. Memory bandwidth for small cached blocks is highly efficient, though large block read and write operations fall into the average tier.

For machine learning workloads, the integrated NVIDIA L4 GPU delivers top-tier performance in prompt processing and text generation for small and medium language models. However, a notable tradeoff occurs with larger models; while prompt processing for a 70B model remains strong, text generation speed drops to the bottom 25%, indicating resource limitations for massive parameter models.

This hardware profile offers a balanced qualitative cost-to-performance ratio for mid-sized graphics rendering, video transcoding, and moderate machine learning tasks. The combination of dedicated AMD EPYC cores, local NVMe storage, and a dedicated GPU makes it highly suitable for database operations, software compilation, and real-time inference of small-to-medium LLMs.
